title: CM 3422 1 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: CM 3422 1 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: CM 3422 1 cassava is a cassava variety. About 10 months to harvest, 30.9 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: CM 3422 1 is a registered cassava variety, also sold or known as Lakan 4 (UPL Cv 10) or Lakan 4. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1999 as NSIC 1999 Cv 15. It takes about 10 months from planting to harvest, with 30.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

CM 3422 1 cassava takes about 10 months from planting to harvest. That is 0.5 months faster than the average of the 42 cassava varieties with a day count, 10.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 30.9 t/ha trails the average of its group, 33.84. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its roots have white flesh. Dry matter is 35.9 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 26.9 percent. Its cyanide level, the HCN content, is low. A low level is safer for the table, while a high level calls for peeling, soaking and full cooking. It is recommended for all purposes (food, feeds, starch).
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** White flesh, dry matter about 35.9 percent, starch about 26.9 percent, low HCN.
**Where:** All regions, best in Southern Mindanao.
Moderately resistant to brown leaf spot and spider mite.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: low cyanide UPLB variety registered for food, feed and starch. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant CM 3422 1 cassava

It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Lakan 4 (UPL Cv 10) the same as CM 3422 1?
items.a: Yes. Lakan 4 (UPL Cv 10) is another name for CM 3422 1, registered as NSIC 1999 Cv 15. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 10 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 30.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of CM 3422 1?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
